verdict.rationale: The delegated-credential core is well documented. The agent enrolls and tokenizes the card (POST /acp/v1/tokens) and gets passkey-authenticated consent for a purchase intent with spend mandates (POST /acp/v1/instructions). It then retrieves a credential bound to a specific merchant and amount (POST /acp/v1/instructions/{id}/credentials), and VisaNet enforces those controls at authorization. The merchant-side checkout handoff (TAP signed payment containers, pre-filled checkout data) and order confirmation are covered only thinly, and the product carries a 'development and deployment' maturity caveat with sandbox-only onboarding. Missing for 10: a first-class checkout-session object or API, a documented order-confirmation flow beyond 'confirm payment outcomes', production availability, and hands-on or independent evidence of a completed end-to-end agent purchase.
